title: Bounded derived residue fibres detect relative perfection for flat finitely presented algebras
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Use unbounded derived categories of ordinary modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and compute derived tensor products by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Let $C\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], meaning quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $k(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$, the residue field of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^j(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ in degree zero and every $j\notin[a,b]$; (2) $H^j(C)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $j$, and for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ one has $H^j(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k(\mathfrak p))=0$ for all sufficiently negative $j$. The lower bound on the derived residue fibre may depend on $\mathfrak p$. No Noetherian hypothesis on either ring is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GHJ, lemma-bounded-on-fibres-relatively-perfect; R-perfect written as pseudo-coherence over A together with finite Tor dimension over R.

proof.text: Assume (1). Taking $N=R$ gives the asserted lower bound on $C$ by the tensor unit identity. Taking $N=k(\mathfrak p)$ gives the asserted lower bound on every residue fibre. Thus (2) holds, with the same bound $a$ in this direction.

Assume (2). Choose a finite polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and let $L\in D(P)$ be the restriction of $C$. The monomials are an $R$-basis of $P$, so tensoring with $P$ takes an injection to the direct sum of copies of that injection; $R\to P$ is flat. It has finite presentation with no relations. The quotient pseudo-coherence lemma applies to $R\to P\to A$ and makes $L$ pseudo-coherent over $P$. Restriction to $R$ does not change the complex or its cohomology, so $L$ is bounded below and its derived residue fibres are those of $C$ as objects of $D(k(\mathfrak p))$.

Choose a bounded-above finite-free $P$-complex $F$ representing $L$, zero above degree $u$. Its terms are $R$-free by the monomial basis, so the bounded-flat K-flat lemma computes $L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k(\mathfrak p)$ as $F\otimes_R k(\mathfrak p)$. Fix $\mathfrak q\subset P$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Applying the flat-localization criterion with module $P$ shows that $R_{\mathfrak p}\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat; it is local because a fraction from $R_{\mathfrak p}$ maps to the maximal ideal exactly when its numerator lies in $\mathfrak p$. Its closed fibre is $(k(\mathfrak p)[x_1,\ldots,x_n])_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, where $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ is induced by $\mathfrak q$ after inverting $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and reducing modulo $\mathfrak p$. The identification sends a polynomial fraction $f/s$ to $\bar f/\bar s$; clearing the finitely many coefficient denominators gives its inverse. The polynomial regularity lemma makes this fibre regular local, of some finite dimension $d$. The complex $F_{\mathfrak q}$ is bounded-above finite-free over $P_{\mathfrak q}$, hence pseudo-coherent, and computes its derived residue tensor over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. This tensor is $T^{-1}(F\otimes_R k(\mathfrak p))$, with $T$ the image of $P\setminus\mathfrak q$. Cohomology localizes: if $d(x)/s=0$, some $t\in T$ has $d(tx)=0$ and $x/s=(tx)/(ts)$; boundaries localize by the same fraction formula. Consequently this tensor has cohomology only in $[a_{\mathfrak p},u]$, using the fibre lower bound from (2), decreased if necessary to be at most $u$.

proof.text: Apply the regular-closed-fibre perfection lemma to the local map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to P_{\mathfrak q}$, the pseudo-coherent object represented by $F_{\mathfrak q}$, and the interval $[a_{\mathfrak p},u]$. Step 3 verified flatness, locality, regularity of the closed fibre, and its derived residue bound. It follows that $L_{\mathfrak q}$ is perfect over $P_{\mathfrak q}$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$. The intervals may depend on $\mathfrak q$; no uniform bound is asserted at this stage.

source.place: Tag 0GHJ, final paragraph, applying Tag 09PC, lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring.

proof.text: The bounded-below stalkwise-perfection lemma applies to the pseudo-coherent, bounded-below object $L$ and the perfect localizations from step 4. Hence $L$ has a bounded finite-projective $P$-representative $Q$, say supported in $[a,b]$ (use $[0,0]$ if $Q=0$). Each term $Q^i$ splits off a finite free $P$-module: choose finitely many generators and split the resulting surjection by projectivity. Since $P$ is $R$-free, tensoring an $R$-module injection with $Q^i$ is a direct summand of a direct sum of that injection, hence injective. Thus $Q$ is a bounded complex of $R$-flat modules, and the bounded-flat K-flat lemma computes $L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ by $Q\otimes_R N$ for every $R$-module $N$. This complex is supported in $[a,b]$. The underlying $R$-objects of $L$ and $C$ agree, so the same interval proves (1) for $C$.
